title: Motions of intellect and of will
source_text: XXIX. Boni autem illi motus, vel intellectum spectant, quales sunt internae illuminationes & cogitationes piae a Deo immissae, ac uno verbo quaelibet illustrationes & inspirationes, quibus mens in veritatis salutiferae notitiam ducitur: vel voluntatem, ut pia desideria & salutares motus atque affectus, quibus immediate voluntas afficitur.
pass_a_gloss: XXIX. But those good motions, either regard the intellect, such as are internal illuminations and pious thoughts sent in by God, and in one word any illustrations and inspirations, by which the mind is led into the knowledge of saving truth: or the will, as pious desires and salutary motions and affections, by which the will is immediately affected.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIX. These good motions concern either the intellect or the will. Those of the intellect are inward illuminations and devout thoughts sent by God, in a word any enlightenings and inspirations that lead the mind to know saving truth.
Those of the will are devout desires and saving motions and affections that touch the will directly.

lemmas.latin: quibus mens in veritatis salutiferae notitiam ducitur
lemmas.gloss: by which the mind is led into the knowledge of saving truth
by which the will is immediately affected

choices.why: Illustrationes are acts of light on the intellect; inspirationes, motions on the will and mind; both are God's direct action.
